cyan-pulse.$description: Cyan Pulse — Blue supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

voltage-cyan.$description: Voltage Cyan — Announcement bar border, decorative code-editor highlights — brighter, more electric than Cyan Pulse, used for outline accents only

plasma-violet.$description: Plasma Violet — Violet supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis.

signal-magenta.$description: Signal Magenta — Hiring nav link, emphasis words inside testimonial bodies — a second accent reserved for editorial moments, not chrome

halftone-blue.$description: Halftone Blue — Soft highlight wash behind cards and decorative code blocks — desaturated cyan used as a tint, never as text or border

deep-teal.$description: Deep Teal — Blue supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

ember-pink.$description: Ember Pink — Inline code-editor decoration, soft illustration tint — decorative, not a state color

alarm-red.$description: Alarm Red — Red supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis

carbon.$description: Carbon — Primary body text, icon strokes, heading default — the dominant dark neutral across the entire UI

graphite.$description: Graphite — Dark surface fill (testimonial cards, inverse blocks), strongest emphasis text

slate.$description: Slate — Mid-tone text, secondary icon strokes, muted body copy

iron.$description: Iron — Helper text, tertiary icon strokes, button label color in dark contexts

fog.$description: Fog — Button label on light surfaces, icon default, disabled-adjacent text

mist.$description: Mist — Hairline borders, input outlines, divider lines

porcelain.$description: Porcelain — Page canvas, default border color, subtle surface separation

paper.$description: Paper — Card surface, elevated panel, code editor body fill

pure.$description: Pure — Inset cards on light gray canvas, button text on cyan fill, modal surfaces

ibm-plex-sans.$description: Primary interface and display typeface. Weight 400 carries body, button labels, nav, and helper text; weight 700 is reserved for headings, large numerics, and the single word inside a headline that needs to be brand-colored. The geometric-but-humanist Plex forms give the UI a terminal-instrument feel without the coldness of a pure grotesque. The 128px step is used for the oversized code-output flourish in the hero.

ia-writer-mono.$description: All code, file names, inline technical labels, the 'Hello!' output render, and monospaced UI affordances. Its slightly humanized monospace proportions pair cleanly with Plex Sans at the same sizes — they look like they were drawn for each other. Weight 700 is used for keywords inside the code editor mockup.
